newsitem.title: USA: Ill. community colleges seek change in tax cap law.
newsitem.headline: Ill. community colleges seek change in tax cap law.

text.p: - Community colleges in Illinois are seeking a change in the state's tax cap law that would allow them to issue bonds without voter approval for life-safety purposes.

Gary Davis, executive director of the Illinois Community College Trustees Association, said Friday that the association was working with lawmakers in the Illinois General Assembly to amend the law and give the local colleges the ability to deal with emergencies within certain monetary limits.

Under the current tax cap law, voter approval is required for all new general obligation bond issuance. In addition, annual local government property tax increases are capped at five percent or the rate of inflation, whichever is less.
"If your boiler has cracks in it, you can't wait for the April election," Davis said, pointing out colleges usually sell GO bonds to pay for situations such as that.
He added the group is also considering a modification of the law to allow community colleges to deal with adverse court decisions.

Davis said the association began to mobilize for the law change in the wake of voter approval of tax caps in 17 counties. He said with tax limitations in those counties set to take affect in January, some colleges have been increasing their levies without having immediate needs for the money. The result, he added, has been an unhappy public.
Tax caps are already in place in six Chicago area counties.
